And the IPO for Anthropic went live this week, boasting the largest offering ever with shares trading around $100. And, in global news, after meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, President Donald Trump is now suggesting he may meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un to discuss nuclear disarmament and the Iran war. The Pentagon is warning Ukraine that drone strikes targeting areas deep within Russian territory are “counterproductive.” Allies in Europe say this advisory doesn’t make a lot of sense. And Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced trip to Venezuela to meet with the country’s interim leader, Delcy Rodriguez.

items.title: Fed’s Cook says rate hikes needed to lower high inflation By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 20 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook on Friday made a case for more interest rate hikes, saying the US central bank’s current policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels she views with "great concern." "In a different environment, the (Federal Open Market) Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury," given how high inflation is and for how long it has been above the Fed’s 2% target, Cook said in the text of a speech to be presented at a central bank conference in Chile. Cook said the quarter-percentage-point rate hike the Fed delivered at its September 15-16 policy meeting was not enough to moderate current levels of inflation. What’s more, "inflation data received since the September rate increase, including reports last week, fail to provide me with sufficient evidence that inflation is returning to a sustainable path," she said. "There is little evidence inflation is declining." Cook, who voted for a rate hike at that meeting, was one of two Fed officials who dissented over the Fed’s decision last month to leave its policy rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Officials at the October 27-28 meeting signaled that inflation remained too high then even as they refrained from action. Regarding her dissent in October, Cook said, "My vote reflected the urgency I feel to tackle inflation," which "has been above target for more than five and a half years, and every additional day poses greater risk that price- and wage-setters will adjust their inflation expectations upward." RATE HIKE EXPECTED IN DECEMBER A wide range of Fed officials in recent weeks have signaled support for more rate hikes, and financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise rates at its December 8-9 meeting and to follow that move with more increases next year. Most Fed officials have made a case for gradual action to lower inflation, arguing that doing so would give the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs. But some, concerned with the most recent inflation data, have speculated that aggressive moves may be needed to bring price pressures to heel. Cook on Friday said the risk of not acting fast enough to lower inflation could bring more pain later. "Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve," she said. "If we fall behind, additional and larger rate increases may be required later to catch up, which could increase stress on our financial system and have unnecessarily damaging effects on American households." The Fed governor noted that financial conditions remain accommodative and are not providing the needed level of restraint on the economy. Cook, however, was upbeat on the economy. She said growth is "strong and accelerating" and that the job market remains "solid."

items.title: Core inflation measures can't escape high energy prices
items.excerpt: Somewhere between 0.2% and 0.6% of inflation in core PCE over the past year is the product of high energy costs, according to a Dallas Fed report. ... Core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) is an inflation measure that is supposed to strip out the cost of food and energy because they’re so volatile — something the U.S. has been experiencing for a while now. But a new report from the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas shows that higher energy prices are showing up even in core PCE. It’s 3.1% higher than a year ago. Fed economists estimate that between 0.2% and 0.6% of that are the knock-on effects of high fuel prices. “Ultimately, energy costs have to work their way through the entire ecosystem,” said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategy director at U.S. Bank. “There's not much that shows up at our house or at our store without requiring a fossil fuel to get there.” Often, energy costs permeate the ecosystem through producer prices — the costs businesses charge each other. “If the transportation company or the the maker of the product — or ultimately the the retail store at the end — if they think they can raise prices and still sell as many units of of whatever, they will pass that cost along,” Haworth said. Diesel — which has been especially expensive — is a major contributor, according to Ed Hirs, an economics lecturer the University of Houston. “Typically, no one can can eat the increased cost of fuel — especially diesel — because it permeates the economy,” Hirs said. “It is passed through all the time.” The price of transportation services has been particularly sensitive to fuel costs. ... “You have to think about airfares. You have to think about buses and rail. Ultimately, they need energy.”

items.title: Trump, while wielding veto threat, sees possible deals with incoming Dem majority | Roll Call
items.excerpt: President Donald Trump said Friday he might get more accomplished with Democrats running the House and Senate than he did in a Republican-led Congress, but his legislative to-do list differs significantly from the incoming majority party. After previously suggesting he could strike a bipartisan immigration deal with Democrats, Trump on Friday added several items to his wish list after returning Thursday night from a swing across Asia, including several that have support with Democrats with whom he’s bitterly clashed before. Speaking in a stuffy James A. Brady Briefing Room for just shy of 90 minutes, the GOP president contended, without naming a single Democratic leader or lawmaker, that members of the opposition party have called him “about two things in particular,” pointing to health care and immigration. “What's happened is I've been called by a lot of Democrats,” he said of the 17 days since Democrats gained dozens of seats across the two chambers. “But people that matter, people that have a lot to do, and they want to talk to me.” But Trump also reminded Democrats that he is more than willing to veto legislation he doesn’t agree with, calling it one of the “extreme powers” of his office and one he might use to bring them to the bargaining table. “So they’re going to send things my way, and I’m going to veto them. And then they’re going to send more things, and I’m going to veto them,” he said. “I think, after a month or so, they’re going to send things, and I’m going to say, ’I’m going to veto, unless you want to do this and this and this.” He predicted House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the likely new speaker of the House, and Sen. Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., expected to become majority leader, would seek deals because both are “smart.” ... Trump went as far as to suggest working across the aisle on health care “may be easier than the Republicans trying to ram it through in reconciliation,” a reference to a fast-track process that allows sprawling bills to pass each chamber with a simple majority — legislation typically needs 60 votes to advance in the Senate.

items.excerpt: ### Beabadoobee Goes Bananas 4 Cats on New Album and Song (Pitchfork) Beabadoobee released her latest record, Pylon, just two months ago, and she’s already announced that she has another one on the way! It’s called Bananas 4 Cats, and Beabadoobee said in a release that she “just needed to write an album like this after Pylon.” She also said it happened naturally, that she felt inspired, and made another album. The announcement also comes with the release of a new song called “No Punctuation” that she’s shared snippets of on social media over the past couple of years, but only recently started playing live. Bananas 4 Cats will be out February 19. ... ### 60th Anniversary Edition of The Doors’ Iconic Debut Album Loaded with Bonus Tracks (Consequence) The 60th anniversary of The Doors’ debut, self-titled album is on the way, and there will be a special reissue to celebrate the occasion. It will come in many forms, including a 2-CD set, two reel-to-reel editions of the album, a picture disc, a vinyl reissue of the “Light My Fire” single, and a disc tracing the evolution of the songs “I Looked At You,” “Moonlight Drive,” and “Indian Summer.” The original record came out January 4, 1967; the anniversary edition will be out on January 8th. ... ### Lindsey Buckingham, Keith Richards, Jason Sudeikis, PinkPantheress and more confirmed as ‘GTA 6’ radio hosts (NME) Grand Theft Auto VI is officially out, and it has a huge musical component to it. There are multiple radio stations you can listen to in the game, and when you do, you’ll hear some famous voices guiding you along. Lindsey Buckingham from Fleetwood Mac, Weird Al Yankovic, Gloria Estefan, The Dare, PinkPantheress, Keith Richards, Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey and her husband Jeremy Dufrene, Chilli and T-Boz from TLC, Michael McDonald, Brigitte Nielsen, and Jason Sudeikis are all DJs on various radio stations in the game. There are also five different episodic podcasts that players can listen to as they go on their gaming adventures. ... ### ‘Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album’ Is Here: Stream the Project Featuring Dua Lipa, Playboi Carti, Lana Del Rey, Cardi B & More (Billboard) The new Grand Theft Auto video game also comes with a stellar soundtrack. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album has 34 tracks on it that spans genres. Dua Lipa, Cardi B, Lana Del Rey, Gunna, Don Toliver, Yung Lean, Future, Metro Boomin, Travis Scott, Fred again.., PinkPantheress, Morgan Wallen, Tame Impala, and more are all featured on the new soundtrack, which is streaming now. Grand Theft Auto VI will also be celebrated with a music festival that is happening IRL. It’s being held in Miami and will have performances from Cardi B, Travis Scott, and others.

items.excerpt: Jorrybell Agoto, the lead actress of Filipinana, died on Tuesday 17 November at 5.20pm, aged 31, after battling lymphoma. ... No premiere date ... Netflix has confirmed that Ginny and Georgia season 4 premieres on Thursday 21 January 2027, with first-look photos released to mark the announcement. The date was announced on 18 November in the US. ... Tyler Posey has joined Netflix’s Harlan Coben adaptation Myron Bolitar in a recurring role across three episodes, playing the spoiled son of a prominent politician alongside series regulars KJ Apa, Colin Woodell and Diane Guerrero. Posey also confirmed the casting on Instagram. ... Netflix has announced the start of production on Patricia, a domestic violence drama written and directed by Juan Diego Botto and starring Penelope Cruz, who also produces through her company Moonlyon. Cruz plays Patricia, a woman who escapes a 12-year abusive relationship and then faces the courts, fearing for her children, with Goya Toledo, Ramón Barea and Dylan Radley co-starring. The film is Moonlyon’s first narrative feature, and it will play in Spanish cinemas before reaching Netflix. No release date has been announced. The story follows Scott Treder, a father who jumps forward in time every morning, starting with a 24-hour jump, while his son tries to reach him. That is the premise of The Traveler, Joseph Eckert’s novel, which Paramount Pictures is adapting with Chris Pratt to star. Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein direct from a screenplay by Justin Rhodes, with Adam Rosenberg and Jules Daly producing. The film is part of Pratt’s new three-year first-look producing deal with Paramount through his Indivisible banner, and shooting is expected to begin in 2027. No release date has been announced. Michelle Monaghan and Justin Theroux are to lead Blumhouse Atomic and Universal’s horror film Sleepover, with Jacob Chase directing from a script he co-wrote with Bryce McGuire, based on McGuire’s short story, and Jason Blum producing. Monaghan replaces Parker Posey, who exited the film two weeks after her casting was announced, and the film keeps its theatrical release date of 8 October 2027. Plot details remain under wraps, and the studio describes it as the quintessential sleepover nightmare.
